options.B: The hospital's interior wall color
options.C: Cultural beliefs regarding health
options.D: Available social and family support

explanation: Internal and external factors like culture, support systems, and personal history deeply affect adaptation, whereas minor environmental aesthetics do not dictate coping capacity. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do we break long-term rehab down into small, bite-sized goals?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any further nursing assessments
options.B: They guarantee that the patient will be discharged within forty-eight hours
options.C: They ensure the insurance company approves unlimited hospital stays
options.D: They prevent client frustration and help maintain motivation during a long recovery

explanation: Recovery can feel overwhelming. Small daily wins keep patients motivated and smiling instead of giving up. You're doing great!

question: A hospital wants shock-resistant drives for mobile nursing carts that load patient charts instantly. Which one should they pick?

options.A: Compact Disc (CD-ROM)
options.B: Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
options.C: Magnetic tape reel
options.D: Solid State Drive (SSD)

explanation: SSDs have no spinning parts, making them super tough for mobile carts rolling down hospital corridors and much faster than old-school hard drives!

question: Why is long-term follow-up education crucial for a woman who had gestational diabetes during her pregnancy?

options.A: She has a significantly increased lifetime risk of developing Type 2 diabetes
options.B: She will automatically develop pregestational diabetes in all future pregnancies
options.C: Her pancreatic beta-cells will continue to destroy themselves over time
options.D: Her baby will permanently require blood glucose monitoring into adulthood

explanation: Gestational diabetes serves as an early warning sign for future metabolic disease, making ongoing lifestyle counseling and periodic blood sugar screening essential. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h8)

question: According to Nigerian client rights guidelines, what is a patient entitled to before undergoing a major procedure?

options.A: A written guarantee that recovery will take less than one week
options.B: Free transportation back to their home village after discharge
options.C: A clear explanation of the treatment and estimated costs
options.D: The personal phone number of the chief medical director

explanation: Clients have a right to transparent information regarding their care plan and financial obligations before treatment starts. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of giving a standard clinical vaccine?

options.A: To provide immediate chemical relief from chronic joint inflammation
options.B: To destroy all existing white blood cells in the patient's body
options.C: To permanently block the liver from metabolizing oral medications
options.D: To introduce safe antigens that stimulate long-term memory cells

explanation: Vaccines give a harmless 'practice preview' of an infection so the immune system can build memory cells and protect the patient later.

question: Why is home delivery not recommended as a default option for every pregnant woman?

options.A: Government policies ban home births completely
options.B: Hospitals prefer to keep all pregnant women admitted
options.C: Unforeseen complications can arise suddenly during labor
options.D: Traditional birth attendants charge too much money

explanation: Labor can become unpredictable very quickly, making facility care necessary for women who develop unexpected risks. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why is it super important to check the publication date of an article before using it for clinical care?

options.A: Patients refuse to answer questions about outdated medical research
options.B: Publishers charge higher fees for journals printed in the current year
options.C: Clinical guidelines and best practices change rapidly as new research emerges
options.D: Older articles are always written by students rather than doctors

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare changes fast. Using old research might mean you are practicing outdated, unsafe nursing care.

question: How is tele-nursing different from general telemedicine?

options.A: Tele-nursing is only performed inside intensive care units
options.B: Tele-nursing focuses specifically on nursing care processes, education, and monitoring
options.C: Telemedicine can only be practiced using written letters
options.D: Telemedicine completely excludes the use of any electronic devices

explanation: Well done! While telemedicine usually centers on a doctor's medical diagnosis and treatment, tele-nursing focuses on the independent and collaborative scope of nursing care.

question: What type of clothing is best for someone working outdoors in areas with lots of stinging insects?

options.A: Brightly colored floral shirts that blend with nature
options.B: Shorts and sleeveless tops to stay cool in the heat
options.C: Light-colored, long-sleeved clothing that fits smoothly
options.D: Dark wool garments to absorb sweat effectively

explanation: You got it! Smooth, light-covered, long clothes protect your skin and help you avoid attracting insects that love dark colors and floral patterns.

question: Which statement best describes the role of most microorganisms found in food?

options.A: They always cause severe food poisoning if ingested raw
options.B: They are exclusively viruses that destroy plant cell walls
options.C: They are either harmless or beneficial rather than disease-causing
options.D: They have no effect on the nutritional value of food

explanation: While pathogenic microbes get a lot of attention, the majority of microorganisms in food do not cause disease and are often useful. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h1)

question: What do we mean by 'out-of-pocket' spending in healthcare?

options.A: Direct cash payments made by patients at the point of service
options.B: Free medical supplies provided by international donor agencies
options.C: Monthly taxes collected automatically by the federal government
options.D: Reimbursements paid to nurses for working night shifts

explanation: Out-of-pocket simply means the patient is dipping straight into their own wallet to pay cash for care because there is no insurance.

question: How does prevention differ from traditional treatment in nursing?

options.A: Prevention stops illness before it starts, while treatment fixes existing problems
options.B: Prevention happens in hospitals, while treatment happens at home
options.C: Prevention uses only medication, while treatment uses talk therapy
options.D: Prevention is only done by doctors, while treatment is done by nurses

explanation: Prevention aims to intercept risk factors before a disorder develops, whereas traditional treatment addresses illness that is already present. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h1)

question: A cook slices raw beef and immediately uses the same unwashed knife to cut fresh tomatoes. What just happened?

options.A: Improper freezing
options.B: Thermal abuse
options.C: Cross-contamination
options.D: Food adulteration

explanation: Correct! Using the same knife without washing it transfers bacteria directly from the raw meat into the fresh veggies.

question: What is the very first thing a healthcare team must do after a serious adverse event?

options.A: Filing a formal police report against the hospital
options.B: Immediate stabilization and care of the patient
options.C: Notifying the international health organization
options.D: Calling a press conference to explain the mistake

explanation: The patient's safety and clinical stabilization always come first right after any unexpected event happens.

question: What does the famous saying 'the dose makes the poison' mean?

options.A: Small amounts of deadly poisons are always beneficial for health
options.B: Any substance can become harmful if the amount taken is too large
options.C: Only synthetic chemicals manufactured in laboratories are truly toxic
options.D: The chemical structure of a drug changes once inside the human stomach

explanation: Even safe things like water can become dangerous if you take too much of them at once. Toxicity is all about the quantity!

question: What is a major financial hurdle stopping many Nigerian women from accessing maternity care?

options.A: Free mandatory transport services
options.B: Mandatory hospital savings accounts
options.C: Out-of-pocket payment systems
options.D: Excessive government health insurance coverage

explanation: Spot on! Having to pay cash directly at the clinic for every single drug or test discourages many families from getting care.

question: What kind of work environment destroys long-term quality improvement?

options.A: A workplace with too many staff meetings
options.B: An environment that uses electronic medical records
options.C: A hospital that provides regular free training
options.D: A toxic or purely punitive work environment

explanation: Fear of punishment stops staff from reporting errors or speaking up about why a new protocol is failing. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is a flatus tube generally left in place for only a short period, such as 20 to 30 minutes?

options.A: To ensure the tube does not dissolve inside the bowel
options.B: To prevent the kidneys from stopping urine output
options.C: To prevent pressure damage to the delicate rectal lining
options.D: To stop the patient from drinking too much water

explanation: Prolonged pressure from an indwelling tube can compromise blood flow to the rectal mucosa, leading to irritation, ulceration, or necrosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the most important daily protection for a leprosy patient whose feet have lost feeling?

options.A: Soaking the feet in hot water daily to stimulate blood flow
options.B: Applying strong chemical antiseptics to unbroken skin daily
options.C: Wearing well-fitted, protective footwear at all times
options.D: Binding the toes tightly together to prevent accidental stubbing

explanation: Spot on! Since they can't feel pain, good shoes protect their soles from everyday cuts, stones, and ulcers.

question: Why is formal accreditation important for a home health care agency?

options.A: It guarantees the agency will never face financial losses
options.B: It replaces the need for any clinical documentation
options.C: It allows nurses to prescribe medications without a doctor
options.D: It proves the agency meets established safety and operational benchmarks

explanation: Think of accreditation as a trusted stamp of approval. It proves through independent review that the agency operates safely and follows recognized standards.

question: You notice three patients on your ward develop the same severe stomach bug within 24 hours. What should you do first?

options.A: Report the cluster to infection control and public health authorities
options.B: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to all patients on the ward
options.C: Discharge all unaffected patients immediately to clear the ward
options.D: Wait another week to see if more patients develop the same symptoms

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Quick reporting helps infection control teams step in and stop an outbreak before it grows.

question: What should you do if you are holding a sterile instrument package and suddenly feel unsure if it's truly sterile?

options.A: Use it only if the outer wrapper looks clean
options.B: Consider it contaminated and discard it
options.C: Wipe the instrument down with an antiseptic
options.D: Ask the surgeon to inspect the item before use

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! Patient safety always comes first, so never take chances with a questionable sterile item.

question: What term describes the presence of multiple chronic health conditions in a single patient?

options.A: Systemic failure
options.B: Cellular senescence
options.C: Acute synergy
options.D: Multimorbidity

explanation: Multimorbidity simply means a person is dealing with two or more long-term health problems at the same time. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h3)

question: What approach should a nurse use when caring for a patient experiencing complications from a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Trauma-informed and non-judgmental care
options.B: Strict detachment with no emotional conversation
options.C: Refusal of treatment until legal charges are filed
options.D: Immediate public shaming to deter future acts

explanation: Patients must feel safe and respected to build trust and accept necessary medical and psychological support. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is the standard safe temperature for storing most routine vaccines in a fridge?

options.A: 30°C to 40°C
options.C: 2°C to 8°C
options.D: 15°C to 25°C

explanation: Always remember this golden rule for vaccines: keep them chilled between 2°C and 8°C so they stay potent and safe to use.

question: A clinic manager wants to know the most common uniform size ordered by new staff. Which measure should she use?

options.A: Mean
options.B: Mode
options.C: Median
options.D: Range

explanation: Uniform sizes are categories rather than math numbers, so the mode helps us find the most frequent size ordered.

question: What is a major limitation of descriptive research designs?

options.A: They require complex laboratory machinery
options.B: They cannot use questionnaires or interviews
options.C: They are too expensive for ordinary nursing students
options.D: They cannot prove cause-and-effect relationships

explanation: Because descriptive studies don't involve testing or experiments, they can only tell you what is happening, not why it is strictly causing something else. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h7)

question: Why is it a big mistake to submerge an infrared thermometer in cleaning liquid?

options.A: It causes the batteries to explode right away
options.B: It ruins the internal electronics and ruins future readings
options.C: It dissolves the outer plastic casing instantly
options.D: It turns the digital display screen permanently black

explanation: Liquid leaking inside will short-circuit the board and mess up the sensitive sensors. Always wipe, never soak!

question: What is the main danger of health workers assuming they know what the community needs best?

options.A: It leads to interventions that the community rejects or ignores
options.B: It causes the government to spend too much money on drugs
options.C: It forces local leaders to step down from their positions
options.D: It immediately stops all outbreaks of infectious diseases

explanation: Ignoring local input results in programs that do not fit the people's actual lifestyle or priorities, leading to failure. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient in skin traction complains of severe leg spasms, and the nurse sees the rope is caught on the pulley wheel. What is the best first step?

options.A: Realign the rope smoothly into the center of the pulley groove
options.B: Cut the traction tape immediately to release all skin pressure
options.C: Administer a stronger pain pill and wait for relief
options.D: Raise the head of the bed high

explanation: You've got this! When a rope slips, the weights stop pulling correctly, which causes muscle spasms. Just pop the rope back into the groove to fix the tension right away.

question: How does a glucometer turn a drop of blood into a number on the screen?

options.A: By taking a photo of the blood drop
options.B: By sensing the skin temperature of the finger
options.C: By measuring the electrical current from a chemical reaction
options.D: By weighing the plastic strip

explanation: When blood hits the strip, a tiny electrical current is produced. The meter reads this current and turns it into the number you see!

question: A patient with suspected Addison's disease is at high risk for which dangerous electrolyte imbalance?

options.A: Hypercalcemia resulting from excess bone breakdown
options.B: Hyperkalemia due to aldosterone deficiency
options.C: Severe hyponatremia caused by water intoxication
options.D: Hypokalemia caused by excessive renal excretion

explanation: Aldosterone is the hormone that normally tells our kidneys to flush out extra potassium. Without enough aldosterone, potassium builds up in the blood, leading to risky high levels (hyperkalemia).

question: When gently pressing on the lower abdomen of a healthy adult, what should you normally expect?

options.A: The urethra should feel tender and slightly thickened
options.B: The urinary bladder is not palpable unless distended
options.C: The ureters should be clearly felt along the flank
options.D: Both kidneys should feel firm and easily movable

explanation: Spot on! When the bladder is empty, it hides safely deep in the pelvis. You only feel it when it is full and distended with urine.

question: How do clinical software apps differ from system software?

options.A: Clinical apps perform specific job tasks like charting, while system software manages the computer itself.
options.B: System software is designed for patients, while clinical apps are for doctors only.
options.C: Clinical apps can only run without an operating system present.
options.D: Clinical apps are physical hardware parts, while system software is purely digital.

explanation: Clinical apps help you do your actual job (like charting vitals), while system software keeps the machine running behind the scenes.

question: How do sperm travel forward through the vas deferens during ejaculation?

options.A: By using their own flagella tails
options.B: By floating downward with gravity
options.C: Through constant blood pressure surges
options.D: Through muscular wave contractions

explanation: The walls of the vas deferens have smooth muscles that squeeze in gentle wave motions (peristalsis) to push the sperm right along.

question: Why are local disaster teams so important when an emergency strikes?

options.A: They handle all federal immigration policies during a crisis
options.B: They are the first responders on the ground before national agencies arrive
options.C: They have unlimited financial resources to rebuild destroyed communities
options.D: They replace the need for hospital-based nursing care entirely

explanation: Spot on! Local teams are already right there where crises happen, making them the immediate first line of defense while distant federal help gets moving.

question: What is a major operational challenge to routine immunization coverage in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of refrigeration units in primary clinics
options.B: Geographic barriers and hard-to-reach rural settlements
options.C: Too many trained nurses available for community outreach
options.D: A complete absence of infectious diseases in the country

explanation: Getting vaccines across rivers, bad roads, and remote terrain to reach every single child is one of our biggest field challenges.

question: What is the main dietary focus when caring for a patient with high blood pressure (hypertension)?

options.A: Sodium restriction
options.B: Zero fluid consumption
options.C: High protein loading
options.D: Unlimited sugar intake

explanation: You know this! Cutting down on salt (sodium) helps reduce fluid retention and lowers pressure inside the blood vessels.

question: A patient can no longer feel hot or cold water on their foot after a back injury. Which pathway is likely affected?

options.A: Corticospinal tract
options.B: Spinothalamic tract
options.C: Cauda equina
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: You got this! The spinothalamic pathway is our body's dedicated highway for carrying pain, temperature, and touch sensations up to the brain.

question: Which of these is a common way nurses check a patient's nutritional status?

options.A: Listening to bowel sounds with a stethoscope for one hour
options.B: Testing daily urine output for trace mineral concentrations
options.C: Calculating Body Mass Index (BMI) and reviewing diet history
options.D: Measuring brain wave activity using specialized electrodes

explanation: As a nurse, checking physical measurements like BMI and asking about daily eating habits are quick, effective ways to spot nutritional issues.

question: What is the main function of social health insurance schemes?

options.A: Pooling resources so healthy people help pay for the sick
options.B: Paying salaries exclusively for hospital administrators
options.C: Making private insurance companies bankrupt
options.D: Eliminating all government taxes on food

explanation: Health insurance spreads financial risk by collecting small regular payments from many people to cover the few who fall ill. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why are peer champions so valuable for sustaining long-term changes in a nursing unit?

options.A: They write all the hospital policies and clinical guidelines.
options.B: They handle the payroll and administrative duties for the ward.
options.C: They model the new behaviors and encourage their colleagues.
options.D: They are responsible for punishing staff who refuse to comply.

explanation: Peer champions lead by example on the floor, making it much easier for other nurses to adopt new ways with confidence.

question: Which common oral side effect should you warn patients about if they are taking phenytoin long-term?

options.A: Severe oral thrush infections
options.B: Permanent tooth discoloration
options.C: Atrophy of the salivary glands
options.D: Gingival hyperplasia

explanation: Long-term phenytoin use can cause the gums to swell and overgrow (gingival hyperplasia). Remind your patients that extra-good brushing, flossing, and dentist visits are a must!

question: What is St. John's Wort most commonly used for?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Mild to moderate depression
options.C: Bacterial respiratory infections
options.D: Severe acute schizophrenia

explanation: St. John's Wort is a popular herb often used to lift the mood in mild to moderate depression, kind of like a natural antidepressant.

question: How does a nurse properly assess a patient's resting muscle tone?

options.A: By asking the patient to push hard against the nurse's hand
options.B: By observing the patient walk across the hospital room
options.C: By measuring the circumference of the limb with a tape
options.D: By feeling the resistance of the muscle during a passive stretch

explanation: Muscle tone is the resting tension of a muscle. You check this by gently moving the patient's limb for them and feeling how the muscle resists.

question: Why can no single agency handle a major disaster completely on its own?

options.A: Government rules forbid any agency from working alone
options.B: Agencies prefer to wait for outside help before starting
options.C: Individual organizations lack any trained leadership staff
options.D: No single agency has all the necessary resources and expertise

explanation: Major emergencies overwhelm the capacity of any single group, making teamwork across various sectors necessary for survival and recovery. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: What happens when someone mixes sleeping pills (sedatives) with alcohol?

options.A: Immediate neutralization of all toxic chemicals in the blood
options.B: A sudden increase in physical stamina and alertness
options.C: Severe respiratory suppression and potential breathing failure
options.D: Enhanced absorption of vital nutrients in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Both alcohol and sedatives slow down the brain. Combining them can make breathing slow down to a dangerous, fatal stop.

question: In safety management, what is considered the MOST effective way to deal with a hazard?

options.A: Using administrative policies
options.B: Conducting safety training
options.C: Elimination of the hazard
options.D: Wearing protective gloves

explanation: If you completely remove the danger, nobody can get hurt by it! That makes elimination the ultimate win in safety.

question: Before you start collecting data for a community diagnosis, what is usually the very first step?

options.A: Securing administrative clearance and mobilizing stakeholders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry
options.D: Treating all sick children with antibiotics

explanation: You always want to respect local authority! Getting permission and greeting community leaders comes first before marching in with clipboards.

question: When writing a good research question, which of these is an absolute must?

options.A: It must guarantee positive results for the hospital
options.B: It must be broad enough to change every nursing policy at once
options.C: It must use complex Latin terms to sound professional
options.D: It must be feasible to answer with available time and resources

explanation: Keep it realistic! Feasible simply means you have the time, money, and access to patients to actually finish the study without stressing out.

question: When taking a patient's history, what is meant by the 'chief complaint'?

options.A: The primary reason the patient is seeking care
options.B: The final medical diagnosis made by the lead physician
options.C: A list of complaints about hospital food and service
options.D: The nurse's personal impression of the patient's attitude

explanation: Spot on! The chief complaint is simply the main issue or symptom that brought the patient through the hospital doors.

question: What is a major worry when identical twins share a single placenta?

options.A: Guaranteed genetic difference in blood types
options.B: Permanent failure of maternal milk production
options.C: Complete absence of amniotic fluid in both sacs
options.D: Unequal blood sharing through connected blood vessels

explanation: Well done! Shared placentas often have shared blood vessels that can cause an imbalance in blood flow between the babies—something we watch out for as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.

question: A patient with damage to the basal ganglia is most likely to struggle with which aspect of movement?

options.A: Reflexively pulling a hand away from a hot stove
options.B: Feeling the texture of an object in their hand
options.C: Smoothing out and coordinating voluntary actions
options.D: Breathing automatically during sleep

explanation: Because the basal ganglia regulate the fine-tuning and coordination of voluntary movement, damage leads to problems like stiffness, slowness, or involuntary tremors. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is measured during an anthropometric assessment?

options.A: Serum albumin levels
options.B: Daily water intake
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Blood pressure readings

explanation: Anthropometry involves physical body measurements like height, weight, and body mass index. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h3)

question: What's the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in healthcare?

options.A: Monitoring tracks activities continuously, while evaluation assesses overall impact periodically.
options.B: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done strictly by hospital administrators.
options.C: Monitoring occurs after a project ends, while evaluation happens before a project starts.
options.D: Monitoring focuses only on finances, while evaluation focuses exclusively on patient medications.

explanation: Think of monitoring as keeping an eye on things day-to-day, while evaluation is like a big end-of-term review to see if you reached your long-term goals. You've got this!

question: How does a soft diet differ from a pureed diet?

options.A: Soft diets are strictly liquid-based
options.B: Pureed diets require more chewing effort than soft diets
options.C: Soft diets contain recognizable food pieces requiring minimal chewing
options.D: Pureed diets allow raw vegetables and nuts

explanation: While pureed diets blend everything into a smooth paste, soft diets still feature actual pieces of food that are simply tender and easy to mash. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h1)

question: What is the best way for a patient to clear the remaining radioactive tracer out of their body after a PET scan?

options.A: Taking a hot sauna bath to sweat out the toxins
options.B: Taking strong oral diuretics prescribed by the doctor
options.C: Eating high-fiber foods to speed up bowel movements
options.D: Drinking plenty of fluids and urinating frequently

explanation: Spot on! Fluids and frequent bathroom trips help flush the remaining radiopharmaceutical safely out through the kidneys.

question: What is the main purpose of electronic communication in nursing?

options.A: Exchanging health data and care details using digital tools
options.B: Replacing all face-to-face contact between staff and patients
options.C: Eliminating the need for any written patient records
options.D: Speeding up personal social media chats during shift hours

explanation: Electronic communication uses digital devices to quickly share patient and administrative information across healthcare teams. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is yellow jaundice showing up in the first 24 hours of life a worry for nurses?

options.A: It indicates that the mother is breastfeeding too frequently
options.B: It is a normal physiological process seen in all preterm babies
options.C: It shows that the infant is experiencing acute dehydration
options.D: It points to pathological processes like blood group incompatibility

explanation: Jaundice on day one is never normal. While regular newborn jaundice can show up later, early jaundice usually means something serious like blood type mismatch or liver trouble.

question: When a patient is prescribed both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, which one should they generally use first?

options.A: Whichever medication is closer to hand
options.B: The corticosteroid to coat the throat
options.C: The bronchodilator to open the airways
options.D: Neither, they must be mixed together first

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first opens up the air passages, allowing the subsequent corticosteroid to penetrate much deeper into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: Which of these weight changes is considered a major red flag during a nutritional check-up?

options.A: Involuntary loss of 10 percent of body weight over six months
options.B: Gradual weight gain due to reduced physical activity
options.C: A stable weight fluctuating by one kilogram each week
options.D: A slight increase in body mass index after recovering from an illness

explanation: Spot on! Losing 10% or more of body weight in half a year is a serious warning sign of nutritional decline that requires immediate nursing attention.

question: Which specific cell type is the main building block found inside a chronic granuloma?

options.A: Platelet
options.B: Macrophage
options.C: Neutrophil
options.D: Erythrocyte

explanation: Macrophages are the star players here! They morph into special shapes to form the core of every granuloma.

question: Why is cutting all fats out of a teenage girl's diet a bad idea?

options.A: It causes an instant drop in body temperature
options.B: It guarantees severe muscle wasting in the arms and legs
options.C: It stops all physical growth and shrinks bones
options.D: It can mess up normal hormone balance and block key vitamin absorption

explanation: Spot on! Healthy fats are super important for making hormones and helping your body soak up vitamins like A, D, E, and K.

question: Why is active observation of a patient's reaction to hospital routines useful for assessing personality?

options.A: It automatically cures any hidden psychiatric disorders the patient has
options.B: It reveals how the person naturally copes with stress and interacts with others
options.C: It replaces the need to ever check vital signs or laboratory blood work
options.D: It gives the nurse exact proof of the patient's genetic family tree

explanation: Watching how patients handle routine stress and staff interactions highlights their underlying coping and relational styles. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h5)

question: What do we call an unexpected injury caused by medical care rather than the patient's actual sickness?

options.A: Latent condition
options.B: Near miss
options.C: Sentinel indicator
options.D: Adverse event

explanation: Don't worry, clinical terms can be tricky at first! An adverse event simply means harm that happened because of medical treatment, not the disease itself. You've got this!

question: Why do nurses always ask for a patient's age during a reproductive health history?

options.A: It is the only factor that determines their legal identity
options.B: It helps spot life-stage specific changes like puberty or menopause
options.C: It measures their overall physical height and weight
options.D: It dictates the exact type of insurance they must carry

explanation: Simple and straightforward! Age gives you quick clues about what life stage a patient is in, from teenage developmental questions to hormonal shifts later in life.

question: As a nurse, why should you immediately report even minor spotting in a postmenopausal woman?

options.A: It proves the patient has a severe clotting disorder.
options.B: It is a classic warning sign of endometrial malignancy.
options.C: It means the patient has stopped taking estrogen replacement.
options.D: It always indicates an advanced, incurable tumor stage.

explanation: Great job! Spotting after menopause is never normal and acts as the main clue that triggers testing for uterine cancer.

question: Which graph is better than a pie chart for tracking patient recovery over several months?

options.A: A pie chart
options.B: A line graph
options.C: A raw data list
options.D: A frequency table

explanation: You got it! Line graphs are your best friend for showing changes and trends over time.

question: A patient with a complex heart condition that a local general hospital cannot manage is most likely sent to which level?

options.A: A traditional birth attendant
options.B: A village health post
options.C: Tertiary health care
options.D: Primary health care

explanation: Teaching hospitals and federal medical centers handle advanced and complicated medical cases requiring specialized experts. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is studying insects (entomology) so important for nurses and healthcare workers?

options.A: It helps track how insects spread diseases to humans
options.B: It allows clinicians to classify bacterial strains accurately
options.C: It improves the treatment of inherited genetic disorders
options.D: It teaches nurses how to manufacture chemical insecticides

explanation: You'll see a lot of vector-borne illnesses in community health! Knowing how insects behave helps us educate patients and plan better prevention strategies.

question: A nurse wants to find articles about asthma in children, but wants to completely leave out studies on adults. Which search string is best?

options.A: asthma NOT children AND adults
options.B: asthma AND children AND adults
options.C: asthma AND children NOT adults
options.D: asthma OR children OR adults

explanation: Using AND narrows the focus to asthma and children, while NOT removes any articles that mention adults. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a correct use of primary clinical space in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Archiving paper medical records that are five years old
options.B: Performing physical examinations and diagnostic assessments
options.C: Providing direct bedside recovery care after surgery
options.D: Administering intravenous medications in a treatment bay

explanation: Clinical space is precious and meant for treating patients! Storing old paper files belongs in a record room, not where active patient care happens.

question: Why are Information Retrieval Systems necessary for modern clinical practice?

options.A: The volume of medical knowledge is too large to memorize
options.B: Paper textbooks are completely banned in modern hospitals
options.C: Computers make fewer clinical mistakes than registered nurses
options.D: Patients demand to see database printouts during rounds

explanation: Medical and nursing knowledge grows rapidly, making digital search systems essential for accessing current facts instantly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h1)

question: What must you often handle first before trying to teach a patient about their discharge medications?

options.A: Discharge paperwork completion
options.B: Full payment of hospital bills
options.C: Severe pain or acute distress
options.D: Complete recovery of normal gait

explanation: If a patient is in terrible pain or panicking, their brain cannot focus on new instructions. Relief comes first, teaching comes second!

question: Why is nurse-led advocacy essential for the prevention of mental health disorders?

options.A: Nurses can influence public policy and secure funding for community prevention programs
options.B: Nurses have the legal authority to pass national laws without legislative voting
options.C: Lawmakers only listen to nurses and ignore all other healthcare professionals
options.D: Advocacy replaces the need for direct clinical care in hospitals

explanation: Nurses use their frontline experience and health data to convince leaders to invest resources into preventive mental health initiatives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h8)

question: Why is it dangerous to stuff a sharps box until it is completely filled to the brim?

options.A: It increases the risk of needle stick injuries for anyone handling the box.
options.B: It makes the container too heavy to lift.
options.C: It prevents the waste from being incinerated properly.
options.D: It causes the plastic walls to dissolve chemically.

explanation: When a sharps box is overstuffed, needles poke out of the top. Anyone trying to close or carry the box risks getting painfully stuck!

question: What is the primary goal of a descriptive cross-sectional study?

options.A: To follow patients from birth until old age
options.B: To prove that one factor causes another over time
options.C: To show how common a health condition is in a population
options.D: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical tool

explanation: Descriptive studies simply lay out the facts—like how widespread a condition is—without trying to prove cause and effect.

question: During which gestational weeks is screening for gestational diabetes routinely performed in uncomplicated pregnancies?

options.A: 24 to 28 weeks
options.B: 8 to 12 weeks
options.C: 16 to 20 weeks
options.D: 34 to 38 weeks

explanation: Insulin resistance typically peaks during the late second trimester, making 24 to 28 weeks the standard window for gestational diabetes screening. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h4)

question: Which ligaments help prevent the uterus from dropping by supporting the upper vagina and cervix?

options.A: Cardinal and uterosacral ligaments
options.B: Inguinal and round ligaments
options.C: Broad and ovarian ligaments
options.D: Sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments

explanation: Correct! Think of the cardinal and uterosacral ligaments as sturdy suspension ropes keeping everything securely in place upstairs.

question: When you visit a patient at home, what is the main goal of building a therapeutic relationship with them?

options.A: Enforcing strict hospital rules in the house
options.B: Taking over full control of household chores
options.C: Diagnosing rare diseases without a doctor
options.D: Promoting health, comfort, and healing

explanation: Spot on! The whole point of building a strong connection with your patient is to help them feel comfortable, heal better, and achieve good health. You've got this!

question: Which of the following is a well-known online database used by nurses to find research?

options.A: Microsoft Paint
options.B: Adobe Reader
options.C: PubMed
options.D: Windows Explorer

explanation: PubMed is a primary online database providing free access to biomedical and nursing research literature. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h3)

question: When you reach the discussion section of your research, what do you do with your framework?

options.A: Calculating the final financial cost of conducting the study
options.B: Evaluating whether the study findings support or challenge the theory
options.C: Listing all the demographic characteristics of the participants
options.D: Providing a biography of the original nursing theorist

explanation: You got it! In the discussion, you check back in with your framework to see if your results back it up or point to something new.

question: A patient with a pacemaker feels dizzy, and the monitor shows a malfunction. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Place a strong magnet directly over the incision to turn off the pacemaker
options.B: Instruct the client to raise the left arm above the head to reset the wires
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider and ensure emergency equipment is ready
options.D: Give a large dose of oral pain medication to calm the patient down

explanation: When a patient feels dizzy and the device malfunctions, act fast: notify the doctor and get emergency gear ready. Patient safety always comes first!

question: What type of organism causes yellow fever?

options.A: A protozoan
options.B: A bacterium
options.C: A virus
options.D: A fungus

explanation: Yellow fever is an acute viral disease caused by a member of the Flaviviridae family. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h1)

question: How do advanced medical technologies generally impact healthcare supply?

options.A: They can improve efficiency and expand diagnostic capabilities
options.B: They automatically decrease the number of patients seeking care
options.C: They always reduce the total cost of operating a hospital ward
options.D: They eliminate the need for skilled nursing staff completely

explanation: Spot on! New tech helps hospitals run smoother and test patients faster, boosting what the facility can handle.

question: What directly causes pain (dolor) during an acute inflammation?

options.A: Rapid freezing of the skin cells surrounding the wound
options.B: Complete lack of oxygen in the local muscle tissue
options.C: Direct destruction of the spinal cord by white blood cells
options.D: Pressure from swelling and chemicals irritating nerve endings

explanation: Spot on! The swelling stretches local tissues and triggers chemical signals that wake up nearby pain receptors.

question: What is the main goal of using a clean delivery kit during a home birth?

options.A: To speed up the progress of the first stage of labor
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing by the birth attendant
options.C: To prevent infection for both mother and newborn
options.D: To provide entertainment for the family during labor

explanation: Simple and crucial—the kit provides clean, germ-free items to stop harmful bacteria from causing infections during and after birth.

question: A hospital unit arranges all high-alert drugs in the exact same alphabetical order in every medication room. What safety design principle is this?

options.A: Complex redundancy
options.B: Punitive discipline
options.C: Manual override
options.D: Standardization

explanation: Exactly! Keeping supplies and medications laid out identically across multiple units prevents confusion and helps nurses find what they need quickly and safely.

question: What mainly determines whether a person with cerebral palsy will live independently as an adult?

options.A: The severity of the physical impairment and presence of associated cognitive or communication deficits
options.B: The specific month of the year that the original brain injury took place
options.C: The total number of siblings living in the same household
options.D: Whether the infant received physical therapy before turning six months old

explanation: How much independence a person achieves depends mostly on how severely their movement, thinking, and communication are affected by the injury.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier that keeps young girls out of school in vulnerable communities?

options.A: High costs of school fees and uniform supplies
options.B: Guaranteed free university placement for all female students
options.C: Cultural preference for educating boys over girls
options.D: Long and unsafe travel distances to the nearest classroom

explanation: Spot on! Free university placement isn't a barrier. Instead, high costs, long distances, and gender bias are the real obstacles keeping girls out of classrooms.

question: Why is the intraarticular route preferred for treating a single inflamed joint?

options.A: It prevents any risk of local infection at the injection site
options.B: It is completely painless compared to taking oral medications
options.C: It completely cures chronic arthritis after just one single dose
options.D: It delivers high drug concentrations directly to the target area with fewer systemic side effects

explanation: Targeting the joint directly keeps the medicine where it is needed most without flooding the entire body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the main idea behind family-centred care when nursing an infant?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to make all home care choices
options.B: Treating the infant as part of a family unit
options.C: Focusing solely on the medical needs of the baby
options.D: Isolating the infant from other family members

explanation: Spot on! Family-centred care treats the baby and the family as one team, making sure you work closely with the loved ones who know the child best.

question: Where can you usually find the meanings of abbreviations or symbols used inside a table?

options.A: On the title page of the research paper
options.B: In the footnotes directly below the table
options.C: In the middle of the table body
options.D: In the reference list at the very end

explanation: Footnotes sit right underneath the table to explain any short forms or symbols, so you don't have to stress searching through the whole paper.

question: Why is Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) described as an ongoing cycle rather than a single event?

options.A: Because medical equipment never breaks down more than once
options.B: Because hospital management loves writing endless reports every week
options.C: Because healthcare delivery and patient needs are always changing
options.D: Because nurses have too much free time during their shifts

explanation: CQI is continuous because healthcare environments are dynamic, requiring constant monitoring and small adjustments to maintain high standards. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which side effect is very typical for ACE inhibitors like lisinopril?

options.A: Severe swelling of the lower legs
options.B: A persistent, dry, hacking cough
options.C: Excessive loss of potassium in urine
options.D: A dangerously fast resting heart rate

explanation: Spot on! ACE inhibitors can cause a buildup of a chemical called bradykinin in the lungs, leading to that classic annoying dry cough.

question: During a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) screening for cervical pre-cancer, what liquid is applied to the cervix?

options.A: Iodine tincture
options.B: Vinegar
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Acetic acid is simply the active ingredient in vinegar! It makes abnormal cells temporarily turn white so the nurse can spot them easily.

question: Which pattern of knowing represents the science of nursing derived from research?

options.A: Empirical knowing
options.B: Ethical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Personal knowing

explanation: Empirical knowing is your go-to science foundation—it relies on objective, observable data and actual research findings.

question: How does placing an advanced breathing tube (like an endotracheal tube) change how CPR is performed?

options.A: Rescuers can give continuous compressions without pausing for breaths
options.B: Medications can only be given directly through the breathing tube
options.C: Chest compressions are stopped entirely while artificial breaths are given
options.D: Defibrillation pads are no longer needed once the tube is inserted

explanation: Once the tube is secured, teamwork gets easier—compressors can keep pushing without stopping to give breaths every few seconds!

question: What term describes the emigration of trained health workers to other countries for better pay?

options.A: Epidemiologic transition
options.B: Resource allocation
options.C: Health tourism
options.D: Brain drain

explanation: Brain drain occurs when a country loses its skilled professionals, such as nurses and doctors, who leave for better working conditions and salaries abroad. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of isolation in a hospital setting?

options.A: To give nurses extra free time during shifts
options.B: To stop harmful germs from spreading to others
options.C: To keep noisy patients away from the main ward
options.D: To punish patients who refuse to take medication

explanation: Isolation creates physical barriers that keep infectious microorganisms contained so they cannot reach other patients or staff. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to discover local food taboos in a new community?

options.A: Fining families who refuse to eat eggs and meat in public
options.B: Publishing a questionnaire in international medical journals
options.C: Reporting the village elders to the federal ministry of health
options.D: Conducting focus groups and talking with key community leaders

explanation: Community assessment is all about direct engagement! Friendly talks and respectful discussions with local stakeholders uncover these practices best.

question: Which dangerous emergency involves blood getting trapped inside the spleen, causing a sudden drop in blood volume?

options.A: Splenic sequestration crisis
options.B: Aplastic crisis
options.C: Megaloblastic crisis
options.D: Acute chest syndrome

explanation: In splenic sequestration, blood pools massively inside the spleen. This causes the spleen to swell rapidly and puts the patient into shock very quickly.

question: In old hospital billing systems, where were nursing care charges usually hidden?

options.A: Pharmacy surcharges
options.B: Laboratory diagnostic fees
options.C: Room and board fees
options.D: Direct surgical costs

explanation: Back in the day, hospitals didn't bill separately for nursing care. Instead, they just lumped the cost right into general room and board charges!

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a referral pathway for home delivery?

options.A: Complying with hospital decoration rules
options.B: Reducing the cost of antenatal drugs
options.C: Ensuring fast transfer to a hospital if complications occur
options.D: Giving the nurse time to rest during labor

explanation: A referral pathway guarantees that the patient can be moved smoothly to a higher level of care without unnecessary delay. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the main reason a patient with acute pancreatitis is kept NPO (nothing by mouth)?

options.A: To rest the pancreas and stop the release of digestive enzymes
options.B: To prevent choking during sudden episodes of severe vomiting
options.C: To keep the bowel completely clean for diagnostic X-rays
options.D: To prepare the stomach for emergency surgical removal

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping the patient NPO means no food enters the gut, which gives the hardworking pancreas a well-deserved break so it stops producing damaging enzymes.

question: What is the biggest danger after a quality improvement project hits its initial goals?

options.A: The hospital running out of paper charts
options.B: Government regulators shutting down the unit
options.C: Patients refusing care from newly trained staff
options.D: Staff slowly slipping back into old, familiar habits over time

explanation: So true! Old habits die hard. Without active effort to keep new practices alive, teams easily slide right back into their old routines.

question: Why is maternal mortality still high in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Infectious diseases have been completely wiped out
options.B: Pregnant women completely refuse to visit healthcare facilities
options.C: Transport delays, money issues, and a shortage of skilled staff
options.D: There are too many modern hospitals in remote villages

explanation: You've got this! A mix of delayed care-seeking, poor roads and transport, and health system gaps contributes heavily to poor maternal health outcomes in Nigeria.

question: Nursing informatics is a cool blend of three major fields. Which ones make up this specialty?

options.A: Biology, chemistry, and health administration
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Nursing theory, public health, and data analytics
options.D: Pharmacology, anatomy, and computer engineering

explanation: Spot on! Nursing informatics brings together nursing science, computer science, and information science to help us manage health data like pros. You'll see this tech in action everywhere on the wards!

question: Which hormones are primarily released by the body during an acute stress response?

options.A: Oxytocin and melatonin
options.B: Adrenaline and cortisol
options.C: Insulin and glucagon
options.D: Thyroid and estrogen

explanation: These major stress hormones prepare the body instantly to confront danger or run away from it. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h2)
